newsitem.title: USA: AEP plans Cook 1 Mich. nuclear unit upgrade.
newsitem.headline: AEP plans Cook 1 Mich. nuclear unit upgrade.

text.p: American Electric Power Co (AEP) said Friday it plans to replace the four steam generators at its 1,020 megawatt (MW) Cook 1 nuclear power plant.
The replacement work will take place during the unit's scheduled 100-day refueling outage in the spring of 2000, the company said in a statement.
"Projected total cost figures for the project are not available at this time. Similar steam generator replacement projects in the industry range from $150 million to $180 million," the company said.
A similar upgrade was carried out in 1988 at the adjacent 1,090 MW Cook 2 nuclear unit. The Cook power generation facility, in Bridgman, Mich., provides about 10 percent of AEP's electricity.
AEP, based in Columbus, Ohio, sells power to about seven million people in Ohio, Indiana, Michigan, West Virginia, Virginia, Tennessee, and Kentucky.
